subject: Post-demo: quantifying shared-capacity impact & next steps
messages:

Date: 2026-12-14T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: quantifying shared-capacity impact & next steps

Hi Priya — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and three asks so we can size the right path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):

- Recap: You want predictable 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for interactive patient-facing flows, plus batch embedding jobs overnight. Our notes: ~80 req/s peak, ~12k tokens/minute during peaks.
- Primary concerns: noisy-neighbor spikes during business hours; strict audit logs for queries; and ability to fail over to a dedicated pool during campaigns.

Can you confirm:
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak 95th percentile token rate (numbers above are our notes).
2) Whether PHI is stored with prompts/outputs or only transient in memory.
3) Acceptable timeline for a POC: would a 48–72 hour dedicated-pool test be acceptable?

Next steps: if you confirm numbers we will:
- Karthik will run a synthetic shared-vs-dedicated microbench and share a short script and results.
- Marissa will prepare an estimated delta in monthly run-rate for Dedicated capacity.
- I will put together a lightweight mutual action plan and a Drive folder for artifacts.

Goal is to make the tradeoff explicit (cost vs isolation) so you can see measurable differences before committing.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: quantifying shared-capacity impact & next steps

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers below and one ask: please include the engineering contact we can queue for compliance.

1) Numbers: steady-state ~40 req/s for interactive flows, peaking to ~95 req/s during campaigns (so your 80 was a good midpoint). Token rate during peak interactive bursts is closer to 16k tokens/minute. Overnight embedding jobs process ~2M records (batched) but tolerance there is higher latency.
2) PHI handling: we cannot persist PHI in cleartext. Prompts occasionally include PHI; the current plan is to tokenize and redact sensitive identifiers before storage, but runtime inference may see PHI in memory. We need KMS-backed encryption for any logs and an option to disable logs for those endpoints.
3) POC timeline: 72 hours for a dedicated pool sounds reasonable. We would like at least one day of steady-state traffic and one day of campaign-simulated traffic.

Ask: can you provide an example measurement script that shows how you detect noisy-neighbor incidents (latency spikes attributed to co-tenants) and what metrics you surface for root-cause? Also please include a rough delta in cost vs. Dedicated so our procurement can start budgeting.

Thanks,
Priya Nayar
Head of Product
HealthSpan

Thanks Priya — adding the engineering detail you requested and attaching the 72-hr POC plan. Karthik prepared a compact measurement approach; excerpt below and the full script is attached as isolation-measurement-script.sh (stub) and our POC plan is healthispan_poc_mop.pdf.

--- excerpt from the microbench approach ---
Purpose: generate two controlled traffic profiles against a shared pool and a dedicated pool and compare latency distributions, token throughput, and tail behavior.
Steps:
1) Baseline: 24 hours of steady-state synthetic traffic matching your estimated steady QPS (~40 req/s). Collect per-request: start/end timestamps, model variant, token count, and host-level GPU util.
2) Campaign spike: 6 hours of ramped traffic to 95 req/s to mimic campaign behavior; look for P95 and P99 degradations.
3) Noisy neighbor simulation: introduce background best-effort jobs on same shared pool to reproduce contention.
4) Analysis: aggregate by minute and compute P50/P95/P99 latencies, token/sec, error rates, and correlation with GPU swapping/KV-cache miss rate.

Key signals we surface: P95 latency (client-facing), P99 latency, token/sec sustained, GPU util by instance, KV-cache hit ratio, and model fallback counts. Attribution: we tag each request with instance_id and correlate latency spikes with instance-level metrics to find co-tenant contention.

Attachments included:
- healthispan_poc_mop.pdf (POC runbook, test windows, rollback criteria)
- isolation-measurement-script.sh (script stub and instructions)

Marissa will follow with cost delta; Markus and I recommend starting the POC on a small dedicated pool that can be scaled during the test if needed. If legal needs the artifact, please loop them in and we will share the Drive folder.

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
